lines.text: Vera, how does a chatbot write its answers?
One guess at a time. It predicts the next piece of text, adds it, and goes again.
So it just... guesses?
Very good guesses. Karpathy's framing: it's a next-token predictor, and the rest builds on that.
lines.say: Very good guesses. Karpathy's framing: it's a next token predictor, and the rest builds on that.

lines.text: Next token? That's me! What's a token?
A chunk of text. Common words get one, rarer words several. Each chunk gets an ID number.
lines.say: A chunk of text. Common words get one, rarer words several. Each chunk gets an I D number.

lines.text: Even “token” got chopped up!
lines.say: Even the word token got chopped up!

lines.text: So I'm just a number?
Then a long list of numbers: a vector. GPT-3 uses 12,288 of them per token.
lines.say: Then a long list of numbers: a vector. G P T 3 uses twelve thousand, two hundred and eighty-eight of them per token.

lines.text: As 3Blue1Brown shows, directions mean things: king, minus man, plus woman, lands near queen.
lines.say: As Three Blue One Brown shows, directions mean things: king, minus man, plus woman, lands near queen.

lines.text: But how does a word know what it refers to?
Attention. Each token looks back at earlier words and asks: who here matters to me?
“The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired.” Who's tired?
lines.say: The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired. Who's tired?

lines.text: The animal. Streets don't get tired.
Attention makes that link. 3Blue1Brown's attention video shows it beautifully.
lines.say: Attention makes that link. Three Blue One Brown's attention video shows it beautifully.

lines.text: Does that happen once?
GPT-2 small has 12 layers, GPT-3 has 96. Each adds a little to the token's vector.
lines.say: G P T 2 small has twelve layers, G P T 3 has ninety-six. Each adds a little to the token's vector.

lines.text: Like a notebook carried upstairs, and every floor adds a note?
Exactly. That running vector is the residual stream, and this guide's name.
And at the top, out pops the next word?
A score for every possible token, turned into probabilities. A dial called temperature makes the pick safer or more adventurous.
Then pick one, add it, and go again.
Who taught it all that?
Training: guess the next token, check the real one, nudge the knobs. GPT-3 has 175 billion of them.
lines.say: Training: guess the next token, check the real one, nudge the knobs. G P T 3 has a hundred and seventy-five billion of them.

lines.text: Over a huge pile of text. Karpathy calls the result a kind of lossy compression of the internet.
A blurry zip file of the internet?
Pretty much. So it can sound sure and still be wrong.
Can I try all this myself?
Every demo in the guide runs in your browser. And in the game, you play the model.
Vera, I was born for this.
Inspired by Andrej Karpathy and 3Blue1Brown. Go watch the originals.
lines.say: Inspired by Andrej Karpathy, and Three Blue One Brown. Go watch the originals.
